chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Yusuf ibn Aqil from Muhammad ibn Qays from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) forbade three [parties] whose transaction becomes one. One of them says to his partner, 'Buy this from your partner, and I will give you an extension [on payment].' They make their transaction one. He said, 'So he should not give him except the equivalent of its silver value which he paid as an extension.' He said, 'And whoever is obligated to him by sale before his partner becomes bound to him, let him sell afterwards whatever he wishes.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on combining transactions for deferred payment in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates the mechanics of 'nasi'ah' (deferred payment) by addressing a common commercial practice where three parties combine transactions to secure an extension, ruling that the deferred portion must match the cash value paid. This narration highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on preventing hidden usury (riba) in complex trade agreements while affirming the flexibility of parties to dispose of their shares before the contract becomes irrevocably binding. The ruling underscores the principle of financial equivalence in deferred exchanges, a key topic in Usul al-Fiqh regarding the validity of conditional sales.
